issues.display_title: Issue #1789: Add `enc` request header to toggle response encryption (default: true)
issues.main_description_html:
Background

Every endpoint that wraps its response through HelperClass::encryptResult() or ResponseEnvelopeHelper::encryptResult() always encrypts data (AES-256-CBC) before sending it to the client. Full list of the 193 affected endpoints: docs/ENCRYPTED_API_ENDPOINTS.md.

Request

Add a request header enc to toggle response encryption per-request:

  • Header absent or enc: true → current behavior, response stays encrypted (default, non-breaking).
  • enc: false → response sent without encryption, data becomes plain JSON (structure {statusCode, data: {messages, ...}} stays the same, just the cry/ciphertext field replaced with raw data).

Suggested approach

  • ResponseEnvelopeHelper already has responseMessages() (plaintext envelope) as the counterpart to encryptResult() — just branch on $request->header('enc') at that same point, no new method needed.
  • HelperClass::encryptResult() doesn't have a plaintext version yet; needs one added (or accept a flag) to reach parity with ResponseEnvelopeHelper.
  • Cheapest place to branch: inside both helpers themselves (accept Request or a bool flag), not per-controller — avoids touching ~190+ call sites individually.

Acceptance criteria

  • enc header read at the helper layer (HelperClass::encryptResult, ResponseEnvelopeHelper::encryptResult).
  • Default (header absent / enc: true) — no behavior change, stays encrypted.
  • enc: false — data is plain, statusCode & messages stay consistent with the encrypted version.
  • Applies to every endpoint in docs/ENCRYPTED_API_ENDPOINTS.md, not just a subset.
  • Update docs (docs/ENCRYPTED_API_ENDPOINTS.md or REGISTERED_APIS.md) to describe the enc header.

Ref: docs/ENCRYPTED_API_ENDPOINTS.md

issues.display_title: Issue #1820: Fix Undefined Array Key "fr" in Tour Template Processing
issues.main_description_html:
Description:

Investigate the PHP/backend error Undefined array key "fr" triggered when user Vincent (#4105, vincent@timeprod.tv) applies the "Festival" template to the "Musilac" tour.

Fix Summary (Commit b7efd1f1)

The GET /templates/menu/match API experienced two main issues causing crashes (Error 409) and missing sub-menus when rendering overlay.json with grouped containers or partial localizations.

1. Undefined Array Key (409 Crash)

  • Cause: When a menu node in the JSON lacked a translation for the active language (e.g., "fr"), the parser executed $pano['name'][$lang] immediately. This triggered a fatal PHP undefined array key error caught as 409.
  • Fix: Added null coalescing ?? string structures in OverlaysClass.php. If the active language is missing, it now falls back to English ('en'), then defaults to an empty string.

2. Missing Nested Sub-Menus

  • Cause: Parent menus/categories (like "STAFF" or "SCENES") are often just label containers with no designated panoramas (id = 0). The previous loop filter $validIds completely stripped them because ID 0 was not found in the panoramas DB table. As a result, all inner sub-children nested inside were discarded alongside their parent container.
  • Fix: Expanded the filter rule in GetMatch.php. The parser will now preserve a menu node if:
    • It functions purely as a structural folder logic (has no id) OR
    • It contains child menus arrays inside its sub property OR
    • Its ID is officially a match in the DB loop.

Note: Upcoming API V2 Requirement
During debugging, we encountered menus with a multi-level nested structure (more than 1 dimension deep: i.e. sub > sub > sub).
The current parser logic still flattens the child elements down to a 1D sub array to prevent production crashes on the current frontend implementation. We plan to introduce a V2 of the endpoint to handle fully recursive JSON payloads natively without breaking legacy frontend apps that do not expect deeply nested structures.

issues.main_description_html:
Description:

When user 56125 completed payment to unlock a virtual tour, a receipt PDF was generated and saved (receipt_3UBPgU4UXotNjjkl03M0nWLq_2026-09-03 01-43-23.pdf), but no record was written to the overlay_audit table. https://gothru.co/moderation/56125/receipt/receipt_3UBPgU4UXotNjjkI03M0nWLq_2026-09-03%2001-43-23.pdf

Research Notes & Hypothesis (Sept 4, 2026)

We investigated the missing overlay_audit issue using user 56125's exact transaction data. Currently, this is strictly a hypothesis because all recent testing transactions processed flawlessly as expected.

However, we identified several vulnerabilities that could lead to this edge case:

  1. Split-Brain Transactions (MyISAM vs InnoDB): Payment tracking tables (cc_logs, cc_purchase, tours) run on MyISAM (no rollback support), while overlay_audit runs on InnoDB (supports rollbacks). If the audit insert fails silently, the payment records remain permanently while the audit completely rolls back.
  2. Bypassed UPDATE Query (user_id Missing Filter): The system verifies existing audits using ONLY tour_key. If a shared/transferred tour already has an audit from a previous user, the script attempts an UPDATE instead of INSERT. Since the UPDATE is strictly filtered by user_id, 0 rows are modified without throwing any error.
  3. ENUM Implicit Mapping (1 vs 1_years): The period variable passes 1, taking advantage of MySQL's non-strict mode to implicitly map to the 1_years ENUM. An unexpected strict-mode trigger would kill the insert instantly.

Next Steps Taken:
Because we cannot currently replicate the exact failure, we have added strict, granular logging to Redis (payment:overlay-audit-debug) surrounding the ToursClass::unlockOverlayV1() mechanics. Once/if this error replicates in production, the logs will capture the exact behavior enabling us to deploy a permanent fix.

issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Implement API endpoints for setting, updating, and cancelling activation/deactivation schedule timestamps for both Hosted Overlay (foverlay) and Google Overlay (goverlay). Supports specifying tour_key to target a specific tour when a moderation contains multiple tours.

Endpoints

  1. Set / Update Schedule:
    • Route: POST /virtualtours/schedule
    • Auth: Required (auth middleware)
    • Payload: 
      {
  "moderation_id": 12345, // accepts moderation_id or mid
  "tour_key": "abcxyz", // optional if mid has only one tour, required/recommended for disambiguation
  "overlay_type": "hosted", // "hosted" (foverlay) or "google" (goverlay)
  "schedule_activate_at": "2026-09-15 09:00:00", // nullable
  "schedule_deactivate_at": "2026-09-20 18:00:00" // nullable
}
  2. Cancel Schedule:
    • Route: DELETE /virtualtours/schedule/{mid}
    • Auth: Required (auth middleware)
    • Query Parameters:
      • tour_key (string, optional): Pinpoints the tour if moderation has multiple tours.
      • overlay_type (string, optional, default: "hosted"): "hosted" | "google" (clears timestamps to NULL for the designated overlay)

Business Logic & Constraints

  • Support both overlay_type = "hosted" and "google".
  • Enforce ownership validation via checkModerationOwnership.
  • Enforce plan access control (Pro / Agency / SubAccount subscriptions via SubscriptionHelper::isProOrAgencySubscription).
  • DateTime validation: Valid format Y-m-d H:i:s, must not be in the past.
  • schedule_deactivate_at must be later than schedule_activate_at (if both provided).
  • Persists timestamps directly to tours table:
    • For hosted: updates fschedule_activate_at and/or fschedule_deactivate_at.
    • For google: updates gschedule_activate_at and/or gschedule_deactivate_at.
  • Manual override check:
    • If user manually toggles POST /virtualtours/active, clear fschedule_activate_at = NULL and fschedule_deactivate_at = NULL.
    • If user manually toggles POST /virtualtours/goverlay/active, clear gschedule_activate_at = NULL and gschedule_deactivate_at = NULL.

  • DTOs: SetTourScheduleDto, CancelTourScheduleDto
  • Actions: SetTourScheduleAction, CancelTourScheduleAction
  • Repositories: ToursRepository
  • Controllers: SetTourScheduleController, CancelTourScheduleController

issues.display_title: Issue #1851: feat(cronjob): Implement Cronjob API Endpoint for Tour Scheduling (foverlay & goverlay) and Email Alerts

Overview

Implement an API-triggered cron worker following existing repository patterns (in routes/cronjobRoutes.php) to process independent activation and deactivation schedule timestamps for both Hosted Overlay (foverlay) and Google Overlay (goverlay), clearing timestamps upon execution and triggering email alerts via Plunk (EmailClass) upon deactivation.

Specification

  • Route: GET /cronjob/process-tour-schedules
  • Query Parameters:
    • dry_run (boolean, optional, default false): Preview scheduled actions without writing to database.
    • type (string, optional, default all): "all" | "hosted" | "google"
    • limit (integer, optional, default 100): Max batch size per pass.

Execution Flow

  1. Hosted Overlay Processing (foverlay):
    • Auto-Activate:
      • Query tours where fschedule_activate_at IS NOT NULL AND fschedule_activate_at <= NOW() AND foverlay_active = '0'.
      • Update: foverlay_active = '1', foverlay_activate_date = NOW(), deactivate_date = '0', fschedule_activate_at = NULL.
    • Auto-Deactivate:
      • Query tours where fschedule_deactivate_at IS NOT NULL AND fschedule_deactivate_at <= NOW() AND foverlay_active = '1'.
      • Update: foverlay_active = '0', deactivate_date = NOW(), fschedule_deactivate_at = NULL.
  2. Google Overlay Processing (goverlay):
    • Auto-Activate:
      • Query tours where gschedule_activate_at IS NOT NULL AND gschedule_activate_at <= NOW() AND goverlay_active = '0'.
      • Update: goverlay_active = '1', goverlay_activate_date = NOW(), gschedule_activate_at = NULL.
    • Auto-Deactivate:
      • Query tours where gschedule_deactivate_at IS NOT NULL AND gschedule_deactivate_at <= NOW() AND goverlay_active = '1'.
      • Update: goverlay_active = '0', gschedule_deactivate_at = NULL.
  3. Plunk Email Notification:
    • For tours deactivated (hosted or google), send an alert email using EmailClass::send() with the Plunk template registered in #1852, passing relevant tour & user parameters.

issues.display_title: Issue #1859: [Proxy] PUT photographers/professional-services -> GoThru Maps backend
issues.main_description_html:
Context

GoThru API New (Lumen 9) needs to expose the photographer "professional services" save feature by proxying to the GoThru Maps backend (Go). No local DB/business logic — forward the request to BASE_URL_PHOTOGRAPHER and relay the response.

Authenticated user id ($request->user_id, injected by existing auth middleware) is used as the upstream gothruUserId. No path param required — matches the existing services route group pattern in routes/photographerRoutes.php.

Upstream contract (Go backend — gothru-maps-backend-go)

PUT /v1/photographers/:identifier/professional-services where :identifier is numeric (gothru_user_id) or slug. No upstream auth middleware; a image_processing role check runs inside the PUT service layer.

  • Request body (missing/null services → upstream 400):
{
  "services": [
    {"icon":"hdr-blending", "name":"HDR Blending", "link":"https://example.com/samples/hdr"},
    {"icon":"object-removal", "name":"Object Removal", "link":""}
  ]
}
  • Validation (upstream, rejects → 400): max 20 items; name required ≤150 chars; icon optional matches ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,100}$; link optional absolute http(s) ≤2048 chars; empty string → stored as NULL. Role not image_processing → 400 "Professional services are only available for image_processing photographers".
  • Response 200:
{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "message": "Professional services saved successfully",
    "professionalServices": [ ...same item shape as GET... ]
  }
}
  • Upstream side effects: full replace (delete+insert, one txn), Redis cache invalidation, async ranking recompute + status revert-to-pending.
  • Errors: 404 {"data":{"error":"Photographer not found"}}, 400 with upstream error message, other 500.

Requirements (this repo, ADR-Domain per docs/ARCH_RULES.md)

Theme: proxy only — no local persistence, validation, cache, or auth logic.

  1. Route — in the existing photographers group (auth applies) in routes/photographerRoutes.php, following the services prefix style: PUT photographers/professional-services. Resolve gothruUserId from $request->user_id.
  2. Service — app/Services/Photographers/<Name>Service.php: base URL from env(BASE_URL_PHOTOGRAPHER) (match existing PhotographerServicesService), use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Http with sensible timeouts. replaceProfessionalServices(int $gothruUserId, array $services): array → PUT upstream with {services:[...]} body; return normalized [success=>bool,data=>mixed,statusCode=>int].
  3. Action — one class (e.g. ReplaceProfessionalServicesAction), one execute(); throw a Domain exception when !$result[success].
  4. Controller — one class (e.g. ReplaceProfessionalServicesController), one handle() using $request->user_id as gothruUserId, return via ResponseEnvelopeHelper. Relay upstream status/error through the Photographers domain exceptions (not-found → 404; 400 with upstream message; pass others through).
  5. Exceptions — add a not-found exception mapping to 404 and upstream-failure mapping where not already present; wire into PhotographersExceptionHttpMapper.

Out of scope

  • Do not re-implement upstream validation (icon/link/name/role). Let upstream return errors and relay them.
  • GET endpoint is tracked in a separate issue.

Acceptance criteria

  • PUT photographers/professional-services forwards the request services body and relays upstream 200 (message + professionalServices).
  • Upstream 400 (validation + role), 404, and other errors relayed with correct HTTP status and message.
  • Follows ADR naming/suffix rules (machine-checked in CI per ARCH_RULES §8).
  • Uses BASE_URL_PHOTOGRAPHER for the upstream URL; no hardcoded hosts.

Result

Implemented and verified in PR: #1862

Changes

  • Route: PUT photographers/professional-services registered in routes/photographerRoutes.php under the authenticated photographers group.
  • Service: app/Services/Photographers/ProfessionalServicesService.php::replaceProfessionalServices forwarding full {services: [...]} replace payload to BASE_URL_PHOTOGRAPHER/v1/photographers/{userId}/professional-services with connectTimeout(5) and timeout(10), connection error resilience (503), and safe root-level error fallback.
  • DTO: app/DTOs/Photographers/ReplaceProfessionalServicesDto.php capturing gothruUserId and sequential list services according to ARCH_RULES.md ADR-Domain standard.
  • Action: app/Actions/Photographers/ReplaceProfessionalServicesAction.php receiving DTO and throwing ProfessionalServicesReplaceFailedException with preserved upstream status code (e.g. 400 for validation or role check failure).
  • Controller: app/Http/Controllers/Photographers/Services/ReplaceProfessionalServicesController.php validating input is a sequential array (array_is_list), mapping to DTO, and returning standardized response envelope.
  • Exception & Mapping: ProfessionalServicesReplaceFailedException registered in PhotographersExceptionHttpMapper (maps to 409 default or preserved upstream status e.g. 400).

    • tests/Http/Controllers/Photographers/ReplaceProfessionalServicesControllerTest.php: integration tests for success replace envelope, missing services 400, non-sequential array 400, and upstream 400 relay.

Summary

Create a new endpoint POST /v1/tours/related-by-cid that returns tours sharing the same CID as the tours being archived — i.e. the tours that will also be archived by the archive cascade worker (which runs outside gothru-new-api). The endpoint is purely informational: it must not perform any archiving itself.

Background

The Archive Tour modal (ArchiveTour.jsx) warns users: "there are other tours with the same CID — they will automatically be archived as well" and shows a related-tours table (Tour Name / CID / Total Panorama).

The archive payload only carries moderationIds (no CID), so the BE must resolve CIDs itself. The archive cascade to same-CID tours is handled by an external worker outside this project — this endpoint only feeds the warning UI.

Request

Uses the same filter payload as batch archive (POST /v1/tours/batch/archive):

{
  "type_select": "selected",
  "moderationIds": ["mid-1", "mid-2"],
  "exceptionIds": []
}
  • type_select: "all" → all tours matching the current filter minus exceptionIds are the archive targets. Note: resolving "all" requires the same query params as batch archive (tags, types, search) — the FE must forward them alongside the body.

{

    "related_tours": [
      {
        "moderation_id": "string",
        "business_name": "string",
        "cid": "string",

      }
    ]
  }
}

  • Return only tours whose CID matches any target CID, excluding tours in moderationIds and exceptionIds (those are already the direct archive targets — the user sees them in the modal; this endpoint surfaces the additional same-CID tours the worker will also archive).
  • Empty array when no related tours exist (FE hides the warning).

issues.display_title: Issue #1884: fix(auth): revoke GT JWT on logout — write token_expired_ Redis denylist
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

LogoutAction deletes the sid session but never revokes the GT JWT. The Redis denylist key token_expired_<token> is read in checkToken() but no code anywhere writes it, so a logged-out token keeps working until its 30-day expiry.

Background

  • app/Class/HelperClass.php:238-252 — checkToken() checks the Redis denylist first, then decodes and compares exp.
  • app/Actions/Auth/LogoutAction.php — deletes the DB session + revokes Keycloak sessions via the Admin API, but does not touch the GT JWT.
  • GT tokens have ~30-day TTLs, so logout is currently advisory for API calls made with the Authorization header.

Tasks

  1. In LogoutAction, revoke the presented GT JWT: write token_expired_<token> to Redis with TTL = the token's remaining lifetime (so entries self-clean).
  2. Verify checkToken() reads the exact same key format (it already reads it — confirm key naming matches the writer).
  3. Review the Admin API revoke call (POST /admin/realms/{realm}/users/{sub}/logout): it kills all Keycloak sessions for that user (every device). With the FE moving to the standard end-session endpoint (post_logout_redirect_uri + id_token_hint, GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4291), consider dropping this call or scoping it as fallback only, to avoid force-logging out the user's other devices.

Acceptance

  • Logout invalidates the current GT token immediately (subsequent API calls with it return 401)
  • Denylist entries auto-expire with the token TTL (no permanent growth)
  • Other devices are not force-logged-out unexpectedly once the per-session end-session flow is adopted

Result

Implemented in #1889 (open, awaiting merge).

  • GtTokenRevoker::revoke() — writes token_expired_<token> (the exact raw Authorization value keyed by checkToken()) with TTL = the token's remaining lifetime, so entries self-clean; best-effort (invalid tokens / Redis outages return false, never throw)
  • LogoutAction — invokes an injectable ?callable $revokeToken after session deletion; LogoutController passes the Authorization header into LogoutDto (the FE already sends it on every request)
  • Task 3 resolved with a decision: the Admin-API revoke (POST /admin/realms/.../users/{sub}/logout) was removed together with logoutUser()/getAdminAccessToken() (dead code, incl. the client_credentials admin-token usage). SSO session termination is now handled solely by the dashboard's end-session flow (GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4294); trade-off (logout from a tab without id_token does not end the SSO session) documented in the PR
  • Verification: auth suite 21/21 (incl. +3 revocation cases); the 2 Photographers/NotifyUpdateDtoTest failures are pre-existing on origin/main; docs/v2/auth/logout.md refreshed to match the new flow

issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Support auto-registration / JIT (Just-In-Time) user provisioning when logging in via Keycloak if the user does not exist in the database yet, matching the existing Google OAuth registration flow (LoginGoogle & RegisterGoogle).

Background

Currently, KeycloakLoginAction::resolveUser() only searches for an existing user by keycloak_sub or email. If no matching record is found in users, it throws UserNotFoundException (which maps to 409).
As noted in KeycloakLoginAction.php:27:

/**
 * Resolves the Keycloak identity to an existing GoThru user, then issues
 * the GT token. Registration (JIT provisioning) is handled separately.
 */

In contrast, Google login (app/Http/Controllers/Auth/Actions/LoginGoogle.php:80-86) checks if the user exists; if not, it automatically registers the user via RegisterGoogle::execute($dataEmail, $googleId, $dataGoogle) and proceeds with session creation.

Reference: Google Registration Flow (RegisterGoogle.php)

When a new Google user logs in:

  1. Inserts into users table:
    • user_name: email or username
    • email: email from Google
    • first_name & last_name from profile
    • google_id: Google sub ID
    • date_created: current timestamp
    • is_active: '1' & verified_email: '1'
  2. Inserts into user_extra_data:
    • user_id: created ID
    • newsletter: '0'
    • is_new: 'Y'
  3. Creates user storage directory:
    • /data/moderation/{userId}
  4. Generates RSS resources:
    • RssClass::addRSS($userId)

Summary

Fix the unsubscribe cronjob (/cronjob/process-unsubscribes-table) where Stripe failed/canceled subscriptions were not detected due to invoice created date filtering, and implement Redis cursor chunking across Stripe, PayPal, and Payflow detectors.

Linked to #1902.

Background & Root Cause

Reported in #1902 (case: user hugogacek@gmail.com / ID: 51572): user's subscription failed renewal in Stripe and was canceled on September 11, 2026 (reason: payment_failed), but remained active in GoThru (subscribtion = 2).

Root Cause:

  • StripeFailedPaymentDetector filtered invoices by created >= now() - 24 hours.
  • In Stripe, created is the initial invoice generation timestamp (~21 days prior, when dunning begins), NOT when it transitioned to uncollectible.
  • Consequently, invoices failing after Stripe's ~21-day retry period were never returned by the Stripe API query, so zero auto-cancel records were queued.

Solution & Implementation

  1. DB Active Candidates: Replaced invoice date filtering with querying active GoThru subscribers (users.subscribtion IN (1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8) with Stripe recurring_profile), then retrieving subscription status directly from Stripe API (retrieve for sub_* / list for cus_*).
  2. Redis Cursor Chunking:
    • Implemented Redis cursor chunking on StripeFailedPaymentDetector, PaypalFailedPaymentDetector, and PayflowFailedPaymentDetector.\n - Redis keys: gothru:cron:*-failed-detector:cursor (Live, Test, DryRun).
    • Controller accepts chunk_size (default 50), chunk_page, and reset_cursor.
  3. Structured & Redis Logging:
    • Real-time Redis run history list: gothru:cron:*-failed-detector:log (last 100 runs).
    • Application logging: [STRIPE_FAILED_DETECTOR_INSERT] and [STRIPE_FAILED_DETECTOR_CHUNK_DONE].
  4. Crontab: Updated gothru-apil-1 root crontab to execute every 10 minutes (*/10 * * * *).

Verification & Live Results

  • Unit test suite: 14 tests in StripeFailedPaymentDetectorTest, plus PayPal and Payflow chunking tests (100% passing).

issues.display_title: Issue #1908: Investigation: Uploaded Panoramas Turn Black & White (Grayscale) Due to External Resize Worker
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

When uploading certain panoramas (e.g. via POST /panoramas/upload from Google Drive / Dropbox), the resulting panorama and thumbnail turn Black & White / Grayscale (W&B) instead of preserving original full RGB colors.

This issue was reproduced and investigated using a panorama from DJI (Model: FC9313) exported via Adobe Photoshop Lightroom Classic:

  • Dimensions: 10585 x 5293 pixels (Aspect ratio: 1.999811..., not an exact 2:1 ratio; width is an odd number).

Related Issues

  • Relates to #1872 (Add Image Pre-Validation & Sanitization Worker for Drive Imports)
  • Relates to #1873 (Fix Floating-Point Dimension Rounding & Color Space Fallback in Image Resizer)

Investigation & Root Cause

1. Verification of the Uploaded File

  • Direct inspection of the source file downloaded from Google Drive (1EM98CqBlJu6XOGZCCvsv22O_NPCX4Y_E) confirmed that the original file is 100% full-color RGB (blue sky, green grass, gravel terrain).
  • The file saved on disk (/data/moderation/{uid}/{cid}/{timestamp}.gd.{random}.jpg) immediately after download was still full color.

2. Evidence: Root Cause Originates from External Worker Outside This Repository

The issue does not originate from GoThru-API-New's download or persistence pipeline, but rather from the external background queue worker in the legacy gothru.co service:

  • Queue: pano_resize_merged (dispatched to RabbitMQ)
  • External Worker File: gothru.co/workers/pano_resize_merge.php (Lines 82–116)

Problematic Code in pano_resize_merge.php:

list ($vWidth, $vHeight, $sType, $sAttr) = getimagesize($aPanoInfo['full_local_path']);

// Checks if pano is exact 2:1 ratio
if ($vWidth / $vHeight != 2 && !($bIsCube > 0)) {
    if ($vWidth % 2 != 0) {
        $vWidth = $vWidth - 1; // 10585 becomes 10584
        system('convert ' . $aPanoInfo['full_local_path'] . ' -resize ' . $vWidth . 'x ' . $aPanoInfo['full_local_path']);
    } else if ($vHeight % 2 != 0) {
        $vHeight = $vWidth / 2;
        system('convert ' . $aPanoInfo['full_local_path'] . ' -resize ' . $vWidth . 'x ' . $aPanoInfo['full_local_path']);
    }
    
    $vHeight = $vWidth / 2; // 5292
    
    // BUG HERE: ImageMagick creates a single-channel Grayscale canvas by default for pure black
    system('convert -size ' . $vWidth . 'x' . $vHeight . ' xc:black /mnt/memdrive/canvas_'.$msgDecode->panoid.'.jpg');
    
    // BUG HERE: Compositing onto a Grayscale destination forces the output into Grayscale and overwrites full_local_path
    system('composite -gravity north ' . $aPanoInfo['full_local_path'] . ' /mnt/memdrive/canvas_'.$msgDecode->panoid.'.jpg ' . $aPanoInfo['full_local_path']);
    
    unlink('/mnt/memdrive/canvas_'.$msgDecode->panoid.'.jpg');
}

Why it turns Black & White:

  1. When dimensions are not exactly 2:1 (e.g. 10585x5293), the worker adjusts dimensions to 10584x5292 and creates a black canvas via convert -size ... xc:black canvas.jpg.
  2. ImageMagick outputs canvas.jpg as a 1-channel Grayscale JPEG because #000000 has no chroma.
  3. Next, composite -gravity north <image> canvas.jpg <image> uses canvas.jpg as the destination/base image. ImageMagick conforms the incoming RGB channels to the base image's colorspace (Grayscale).
  4. The output is written directly over $aPanoInfo['full_local_path'], permanently stripping color from the original image and downstream thumbnails.

Result & Evidence

  • Before Worker: /data/moderation/50214/.../*.jpg is RGB (Is B&W: False, Saturation avg: 62.6).
  • After Worker: https://img.gothru.org/50214/.../*_thumb.jpg and *.jpg become pure Grayscale (Is B&W: True, $R=G=B$ across all pixels).
  • Video Proof:

This is the result when no request is sent to RabbitMQ:

2026-09-17.14-41-29.mp4

Workaround Implemented in GoThru-API-New

Commit: ac3dde2cc on main:

  1. Bypassed Worker for Target User:
    • For muhamad.rifky.dev@gmail.com (UID 50214), UploadPanoramaAction and PanoResizeQueueService bypass dispatching to RabbitMQ pano_resize_merged.
  2. Local GD Thumbnail Generation:
    • Generates thumbnail directly via PanoImageHelper::generateThumbnail() (PHP GD), preserving full RGB color space.
  3. Database Local Path Consistency:
    • Sets thumb_local_path to /data/moderation/{uid}/{cid}/ so thumbnails are served accurately without hitting broken worker output.
  4. Unit Tests:
    • Added test_skips_resize_queue_for_excluded_user covering the bypass behavior.

Permanent Fix Recommendation for gothru.co

In gothru.co/workers/pano_resize_merge.php (and related workers using xc:black), enforce sRGB and TrueColor on the canvas:

convert -size {$vWidth}x{$vHeight} xc:black -colorspace sRGB -type TrueColor /mnt/memdrive/canvas_{$panoid}.jpg

or use magick composite -colorspace sRGB ....
